verdict.rationale: Firebase's own Local Emulator Suite lets you run Firestore, Realtime Database, Storage, Auth, Hosting, Functions and more locally. The docs say you can connect your app to these emulators to run integration tests or QA without touching production data, and the Test SDK can flush the local database between tests. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, GA status for the Functions/Pub/Sub/Extensions emulators (still beta), and evidence that AI agents (e.g., via the MCP server) can target the emulators.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: This means you can connect your app directly to these emulators to perform integration testing or QA without touching production data.

The Firebase Local Emulator Suite is a set of advanced tools for developers looking to build and test apps locally using Cloud Firestore, Realtime Database, Cloud Storage for Firebase, Authentication, Firebase Hosting, Cloud Functions (beta), Pub/Sub (beta), and Firebase Extensions (beta).
The Test SDK provides several convenience methods for loading Security Rules, flushing the local database between tests
you can install and manage Firebase Extensions in a safe local environment and better understand their capabilities while minimizing billing costs
